questions.solution:

• The subject of the sentence is **"The board"**, which is treated as a singular collective noun in standard English usage.

• Example: The team **is** preparing for the big game.
 
• However, in British English, they are sometimes treated as plural if the focus is on the members of the group acting individually.
 
 
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:**
 
 
• It is crucial to ensure that the verb matches the subject in both number and form.
 
• Example: The committee **has** made its decision (singular).

questions.question:

The renowned professor had been given a standing ovation by the students after her powerful lecture.

options.text: The students had been giving the renowned professor a standing ovation after her powerful lecture.

After her powerful lecture, the students had given the renowned professor a standing ovation.
After her powerful lecture, a standing ovation had been given to the renowned professor by the students.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**, where the subject (the renowned professor) is the receiver of the action.
 
• To convert the sentence to the **active voice**, we need to make the doer of the action (students) the subject of the sentence.
 
• The original sentence is: *The renowned professor had been given a standing ovation by the students after her powerful lecture.*
 
• In the active voice, the sentence becomes: *After her powerful lecture, the students had given the renowned professor a standing ovation.*
 
• This rearranges the sentence to correctly follow the structure of an active voice sentence: Subject (students) + verb (had given) + object (the renowned professor).

Correct sentence: *After her powerful lecture, the students had given the renowned professor a standing ovation*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active Voice:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + verb + object.
 
• **Example:** The students wrote an essay.
 
• **Usage:** The subject performs the action.
 
 
 
• **Passive Voice:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Object + verb (to be) + past participle + by + subject.
 
• **Example:** An essay was written by the students.
 
• **Usage:** The focus is on the action or the receiver of the action.
 
 
</ul

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **future perfect tense**, which describes actions that will be completed before a specific point in the future.
 
• The passive voice transformation of a sentence in the future perfect tense follows the structure: **Object + will have been + past participle + (by + subject).**
 
• Here, the active sentence is: *"They will have built the bridge by next year."*
 
• In the passive voice:
 
 
• The object of the active sentence, "the bridge," becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The verb "will have built" changes to "will have been built" to indicate the passive voice.
 
• The subject of the active sentence, "they," is included in the passive sentence with "by them."
 
 

Correct sentence: *The bridge will have been built by them by next year*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active voice to passive voice transformation rules:**
 
 
• Identify the object of the active sentence and make it the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• Change the verb form according to the passive voice structure, keeping the tense intact.
 
• Include the subject of the active sentence after the verb, preceded by "by," if necessary.
 
 
 
• **Examples of future perfect tense transformation:**
 
 
• Active: She will have completed the project by tomorrow. 
Passive: The project will have been completed by her by tomorrow.
 
• Active: They will have finished the homework. 
Passive: The homework will have been finished by them.

questions.question: Pipe P can fill a tank in 12 hours, and pipe Q can empty the same tank in 18 hours. If both pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the tank be full?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe P fills tank in 12 hours

Pipe Q empties tank in 18 hours

**Formula used:**

LCM = Total work

Efficiency = Work / Time

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM of 12 and 18 = 36 (Total work)

⇒ P efficiency = 36 / 12 = 3 units/hour

⇒ Q efficiency = 36 / 18 = 2 units/hour (emptying)

⇒ Net efficiency = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Time = 36 / 1 = 36 hours

**∴ Tank will be full in 36 hours**

questions.question: -From October 1, 2023, which organisation has introduced the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**European Union**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **European Union (EU)** introduced the **Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)** on **October 1, 2023**, as part of its broader commitment to reducing carbon emissions and addressing climate change. 
• CBAM is a critical policy under the **European Green Deal**, aimed at ensuring that the cost of carbon emissions is factored into the price of imported goods. 
• The mechanism applies to carbon-intensive products such as **cement, aluminum, steel, fertilizers, electricity, and hydrogen**, among others, imported into the European Union. 
• The primary goal of CBAM is to prevent **carbon leakage**, which occurs when companies relocate their production to countries with less stringent climate policies, undermining global climate goals. 
• Initially, the mechanism will operate in a **transitional phase** until 2026, focusing on reporting emissions without imposing financial obligations. Full implementation with a monetary carbon levy is set to begin thereafter. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **European Green Deal:** 
• Launched in **2019**, the European Green Deal is the EU's roadmap to make Europe the first **climate-neutral continent** by **2050**. 
• It includes policies targeting **clean energy, sustainable industry, and biodiversity**, along with the CBAM to address carbon leakage. 
• **Carbon Leakage:** 
• Occurs when industries relocate production to regions with **weaker climate policies**, causing an increase in global emissions rather than reducing them. 
• CBAM aims to **level the playing field** by imposing a carbon cost on imports equivalent to the EU’s carbon price. 
• **Implementation Process:** 
• During the **transitional phase (2023-2026)**, importers are required to report the embedded emissions of their goods, but no financial payments are demanded. 
• From **2026 onwards**, importers will need to purchase **CBAM certificates** to account for the carbon emissions of imported goods. 
• **Global Implications:** 
• CBAM has raised concerns among **developing countries** and trade partners, as it could impact their export competitiveness. 
• It encourages other countries to adopt **similar carbon pricing mechanisms** to align with global climate goals. 
• **Comparison with Other Initiatives:** 
• While CBAM is specific to the EU, similar initiatives are being discussed globally to address **carbon emissions in trade**. 
• For example, the **United States** has proposed a **Clean Competition Act** with similar objectives.

 __ 
• **Depreciation of capital** refers to the gradual reduction in the value of physical assets such as **machinery, equipment, and infrastructure** due to factors like wear and tear, obsolescence, and time. 
• **Replacement investment** is the investment made to replace or restore depreciated capital goods. This ensures that the production capacity of a business remains intact and efficient. 
• In the context of wear and tear during the production process, replacement investment is directly related to the **depreciation** of capital goods, as these assets need to be replaced or repaired periodically to maintain operational efficiency. 
• The wear and tear of machinery and equipment is a natural consequence of their continuous usage. This is accounted for as **depreciation** in financial records, emphasizing the need for regular replacement investment.

 __

• It is an **accounting method** used to allocate the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life. 
• Common methods of depreciation include **straight-line depreciation** and **declining balance depreciation**. 
• Depreciation helps businesses account for the **gradual loss of value** of their assets. For example, a machine costing **$100,000** with a useful life of **10 years** will depreciate by **$10,000 per year** under the straight-line method.

• The term **'Atman'** is a core concept in the **Upanishads**, referring to the **inner self or soul**, and is distinct from the physical body, mind, and emotions.

• The **Atman** is considered **eternal and unchanging**, representing the true essence of an individual beyond material existence.

• The **Upanishads** describe the Atman as being **identical to Brahman**, the ultimate cosmic reality, emphasizing the unity between the individual soul and the universal spirit.

• Philosophical discussions in the **Upanishads** often revolve around understanding the Atman and its relationship with Brahman, aiming for spiritual liberation (**Moksha**).

• The concept of Atman is central to **Advaita Vedanta**, a non-dualistic school of Hindu philosophy, which posits that realization of Atman as Brahman leads to enlightenment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Major Upanishads include the **Chandogya Upanishad, Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, Katha Upanishad, and Mundaka Upanishad**.

• They focus on spiritual and philosophical teachings, exploring topics like **reality, self, ethics, and liberation (Moksha)**.

• **Relation Between Atman and Brahman:**

• The **Upanishads** assert that the individual soul (**Atman**) is not separate from the universal spirit (**Brahman**).

• Realizing this unity is key to achieving **Moksha**, or liberation from the cycle of **birth and death (Samsara)**.

• **Philosophical Schools of Thought:**

• **Advaita Vedanta:** Proposes non-dualism, where Atman and Brahman are one and the same.

• **Dvaita Vedanta:** Emphasizes dualism, where Atman and Brahman are distinct.

• **Vishishtadvaita Vedanta:** Suggests qualified non-dualism, where Atman and Brahman are distinct yet interrelated.

• **Concept of Moksha:**

• **Moksha** refers to liberation from the cycle of **Samsara** (birth, death, and rebirth).

• Understanding the true nature of Atman as Brahman is essential for attaining **Moksha**.

• **Other Options Explained:**

• **Ritual fire:** While significant in Hindu rituals, it does not refer to Atman.

• **Sacred chant:** Mantras and chants are important in spiritual practices but are distinct from the concept of Atman.
